summary: Coffee County tower that the Tennessee tower list marks removed; the list gives 1,208 ft and no build date, staffing or fire history.

facts.status_note: The Tennessee tower list marks the tower removed. No source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: The Tennessee tower list marks the tower removed.

evidence.supports: Farrar Hill tower in Coffee County at 1,208 ft, marked removed
Tower number 5-6 is a district-tower number from a 1976 list
evidence.quote: Numbers in the table (e.g., 4-7) are state forest tower numbers (district-tower) from 1976 list of towers

evidence.supports: Civilian Conservation Corps erected 98 lookout towers in Tennessee, 1933 to 1941
evidence.quote: From 1933 to 1941, the Civilian Conservation Corps erected 98 lookout towers in Tennessee.

evidence.supports: Towers were part of the Division of Forestry's fire detection network; many removed or awaiting demolition after disuse or lease expiry
evidence.quote: Many of the 208 fire lookout towers once part of TDF’s fire detection network have been removed or are awaiting demolition as a result of disuse or the expiration of lease agreements with private property owners.

evidence.supports: Statewide, most tower locations are now private property
evidence.quote: Many have been removed, and most locations are now private property

evidence.supports: The list advises people not to climb the towers, which often have steps removed or rotten
evidence.quote: You are advised not to climb the towers, often steps have been removed or are rotten

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers MPS
sources.publisher: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

notes_for_editor: Only two sources: the Tennessee Landforms tower list (table row reads Farrar Hill, 1208', Coffee, 5-6 removed) and the NRHP study, which says nothing about this tower specifically. No build date, staffing, fire, photo or access source found. Wikipedia's Farrar Hill, Tennessee article has no tower mention. The brief's elevation (368.2 m) matches the list's 1208 ft. Story is short because the evidence is short; a Coffee County newspaper or county history would be the next place to look.
